 Print Saransh Jain (Image credit: X) NEW DELHI: Saransh Jain has made the most of his return to domestic cricket after missing out on India's squad for the Test series against New Zealand. The Madhya Pradesh spinner picked up seven wickets to bowl Bihar out for just 99 in their Ranji Trophy match on Monday. Jain finished with figures of 7/40, his best bowling performance in a first-class innings. His effort left Bihar's batting line-up struggling and put Madhya Pradesh in a strong position. The 33-year-old had made his India debut in the second Test against Sri Lanka earlier this year. But he did not find a place in the squad for the upcoming two-match series against New Zealand. Watch Mitchell Santner press conference: New Zealand captain on India's win, missed chances & more Bihar batters struggle against Jain
 Jain took seven wickets in 13 overs, giving away 40 runs and bowling one maiden. Bihar were all out for 99 in just 30.3 overs. The spinner began by dismissing Ayush Loharuka, captain Sakibul Gani and Akash Raj. He continued to trouble the batters, removing Raghuvendra Pratap Singh, Aditya Raj, Suraj Kashyap and Himanshu Singh to complete his seven-wicket haul. Join conversation

 India debut, but no place in New Zealand squad
 Jain earned his first India cap at the age of 33 when he played in the second Test against Sri Lanka earlier this year. He became India's oldest Test debutant since Robin Singh in 1998. RJD Jamshedji remains India's oldest Test debutant, having made his debut at 41 years and 27 days. Jain played in the second Test (from August 23 to 27) and took three wickets. That remains his only appearance for India so far. Jain has represented Madhya Pradesh in 59 first-class matches. He has scored 2,312 runs and taken 195 wickets at an average of 28.23.
